THE REPORT DOES NOT EXIST. /home/nickmagus/krabby/krabby-research/parkour/parkour_tasks/parkour_tasks/crab_hex_omni_task/experiments/2026-09-30_rl_algorithm_review/ holds only DOSSIER.md (16:18) and artifacts/. I watched the path from 17:03 to 18:26 (inotify-style loop plus two 30-min Monitor watches), searched every checkout, worktree (.claude/worktrees/keen-bhaskara-c448d0) and session scratchpad under /tmp/claude-1000, and checked the two live claude processes: one is this session, the other's only shell child is the side-bisect queue watcher (`until grep -qE "EVENT C_40 |STOP controls..."`). No process is drafting a report. The user must not act on a report that has not been written and checked; issue R0 below is the blocking one.

What I could do instead: I read the dossier and the literature review in full, verified the code claims the five critiques make (the report was to be built from them), and re-derived their arithmetic. Result: the critiques' load-bearing numbers reproduce (side-bisect σ at it 600: fast arms ≤ 1.700, two-direction arms ≥ 1.704, phantom arms overlap, from artifacts/omni_stroke_side/tb_arms.json; 2×2/3-seed MDEs 1.85σ main, 2.61σ cell-vs-incumbent, 3.70σ interaction by noncentral t; Fisher 3/3-vs-0/3 two-sided p = 0.10, 5/5 p = 0.008; lit §15 rung sum 51.9 GPU-h; GAE horizon 16.8 steps = 0.34 s; bound-loss calibration (11−1.1)²×18 = 1,764). Their code claims also hold: the action history stores clipped actions (parkour_actions.py:348-351) so the PR #2019 audit in lit §2 is already answered; action_rate is the UNSQUARED L2 norm on the delayed clipped action (parkour_isaaclab/envs/mdp/rewards.py:336-343), contradicting lit §4's "squared ... near-constant" wording; a `schedule='fixed'` resume silently keeps the checkpoint's Adam LR (ppo_with_extractor.py:377-404 writes param_group lr only in the adaptive branch; :559-560 restores learning_rate only for adaptive; runner :737 restores the optimizer state; :543 logs alg.learning_rate not the applied lr); the deploy exporter substitutes the estimator and returns the raw actor output with no clamp (scripts/rsl_rl/exporter.py:112-130); replay_reward_economy.py:100 clips rods at ±4.8, so the dossier §4.4(a) creeper action_rate figures (−0.516/−0.198) are from a known clip bug (commit 3714934c fixed only the sibling clock tool); forward rsl_rl_ppo_cfg.py:134-145 hard-codes use_data_augmentation=False, so rung 6's augmentation arm is unreachable without code. One critique claim is NOT supported: the switch-advocate's "SAC surpasses PPO on humanoids" — the arXiv 2605.24975 abstract says only that the method "closes the performance gap with PPO entirely" (parity), so the literature review's "matched PPO" wording should stand.

CENTRAL VERDICT (keep PPO; fix the construction; defer family swaps): I AGREE, with two amendments the report must carry. (1) "Fix the construction" is justified by learning-signal hygiene, motion quality and hardware chatter (2.23 sign flips/dim/s on non-backdrivable rods), NOT by an expected task-metric gain: the dossier's own scoreboard attributes no task metric to the optimizer (§4.8 :680-692; :993 "absent either way"), saturation is 0.941-0.978 in fast and slow side heads alike (:302, :515), the only optimizer change ever run (M1) cost turn facing 0.610→0.510 (MQ REPORT.md D05), and the levers that moved task metrics were reward (+0.33 facing), curriculum (+0.20), the fa mirror/scalar obs (side 0.084→0.184-0.217 m/s) and morphology (obstacles 2-3×). (2) The strongest single action for a task metric is structural, not algorithmic: canonical training / the M_y canonicaliser, already proven at deploy on 4/4 fast heads (|L−R| ≤ 0.006). A family swap (TD3-lean, FPO++) is not warranted now: no legged off-policy result exists at ≤256 envs, and the two-hand failure has a no-training structural fix; but the swap-cost objections in dossier §6 should be corrected (a 259-dim non-history replay slice is ≈0.54 GB per 1,024 transitions/env at 256 envs, not 9.2 GB; a PPO-schema checkpoint can be emitted by any learner), so that condition (b) of lit §15 is a 10-minute timing inside rung 1 rather than a gate.

If the report, when written, carries the lit review's §15 ladder unmodified, issues R1-R13 apply to it verbatim; if it adopted the critiques, R2, R7, R8 and R14 are the places where the critiques conflict with each other and the report must show which it chose and why.

issues.issue: The reward economy confounds any bounded-head arm: reward_action_rate reads the delayed, clipped executed action (during training the noisy sample), so a saturated mean hides its exploration noise from the term and a bounded mean cannot. Rung 2 as written measures head + reward together. The lit review also mis-describes the term as 'squared ... near-constant under saturation'.
issues.evidence: rewards.py:337-343: `torch.norm(prev[1]-prev[0])`, squared only under KRABBY_ACTION_RATE_SQ (default off); weight −0.3 on W. raw_actions = 1-step-delayed clipped action (parkour_actions.py:348-357; wrapper clamp vecenv_wrapper.py:134-136). Two independent CPU Monte Carlos agree: bounding W's means to ±1.1 raises the training-time cost by +0.15/+0.55/+0.83/+0.99 per s at σ 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0 (action-path audit) vs 0.68-1.44/s (skeptic), against W's whole net return ≈1.17/s and a fast-vs-slow side-gait margin of +0.25 to +0.43/s (ROOT_CAUSE.md:258-268). In-repo, smoothness taxes traded completion monotonically (gait_formation_v2 CHANGELOG L2 0.81, L3 0.64 vs 0.90-0.94; 'churn is load-bearing').

Log deterministic ‖Δclip(μ)‖ beside the sampled term. Pass the offline reward-replay gate in a sampled-σ mode before any GPU run. Correct lit §4: the default term is the unsquared L2 norm and is not constant (≈0.34/s logged on W).

issues.evidence: Noncentral-t MDE at 80 % power, α 0.05 two-sided, pooled df 8: main effect 1.85σ, combined-vs-incumbent 2.61σ, interaction 3.70σ (re-derived). Single-seed MDE turn facing 0.145, move_turn 0.180 (facing CHANGELOG :46-47); pooling 3 seeds gives ≈0.084 / 0.104 — the same order as the largest curriculum effect (+0.20). Fisher 3/3 vs 0/3 two-sided p = 0.10; the review's own rule is 5 seeds when formation decides (:451-453). All 6 omni clock-held t3 runs formed (fwd survival 0.49-0.96; DOSSIER :403). ':567-569 the two knobs must be co-varied: lowering σ alone cannot produce an interior mean ... a bound alone at σ 2.0 leaves the clip binding' — i.e. half the 2×2 is pre-declared dead (≈7 GPU-h). Gates list 'saturation share and P10, sign flips, formation rate over seeds, tracking and side-speed class' — no F/F_mt block, no obstacle read; and saturation share is circular under a bound loss (it penalises |μ| > 1.1 by construction).
issues.fix: Run the diagonal cell vs a fresh incumbent (5 seeds each, or group-sequential 3→5 with a pre-registered continuation zone); off-diagonals only to explain a diagonal task win. Split manipulation checks (saturation < 0.5, σ below cap, executed-KL share; n = 2 suffices) from outcomes (side ratio class shift ≥ 0.10; Q block; T and F as estimation with CIs; survival as a catastrophe tripwire, not a non-inferiority guard). Use the bound loss, not tanh, as the head factor (no checkpoint/exporter/eval change). Hold entropy_coef constant across the head factor: entropy 0 removes a tanh head's only inward force.

issues.location: lit review §15 rung 2 arm text (:562-566) and rung 4 (:576-579); implementation critique F1/F4/F11; design critique F8
issues.issue: Several arm and gate definitions are under-specified in ways that would make runs uninterpretable: the tanh head's placement and checkpoint marker; the σ 'factor' bundling four knobs incl. a mean-side last-layer init; eval action metrics that change meaning between saturated and bounded heads; num_envs hard-coded in the driver and pinned by a test; eval process-state artefacts the size of the margins.
issues.evidence: tanh_encoder_output only appends nn.Tanh to the mean with no log-det (actor_critic_with_encoder.py:86-87); a runner-side squash flag adds no parameters so strict load passes and evals rebuild from the registry (eval_crab_hex_gait.py:639; EVAL_CARRY run_phases.py:169-179 carries no runner knob) — the head would be evaluated as clip(u) silently. Episode-level action block computes action_rate/reversals on raw pre-clip means (report.py:294-299 → metrics.py:929-976); the 2.23 flips/dim/s counts raw-μ sign flips with no deadzone (ANALYSIS_M1_saturation.md:44-48). NUM_ENVS = {'rl': '256'} (omni run_phases.py:71, used at :1297) inside the seam pinned by tests/unit/test_crab_hex_omni_gate.py:2542-2547; the generator drops batch % num_mini_batches rows (rollout_storage.py:227-228). Any os.environ write after Kit start flips evals 0.79↔0.75 (memory eval-process-state-sensitivity.md).
issues.fix: If tanh is used at all: squash inside Actor.forward with a persistent `squash_flag` buffer, forward_pre_squash for the Gaussian, KRABBY_ACTION_SQUASH in AGENT_KNOBS, EVAL_CARRY and the manifest; otherwise use the bound loss (≈20 lines per the audited M1b spec). Fix every arm value before launch (bound 1.1, coef 1e-4→1e-3 ramp, σ init 0.8 via tanh-bounded log-std to [ln 0.05, ln 2], entropy 0.0025 no fallback, last-layer init in all cells or none). Score chatter on executed actions with |a| ≥ 0.5 deadzone; make saturation gates read executed near-bound share plus pre-squash |u|. Add KRABBY_NUM_ENVS + KRABBY_PPO_MINIBATCHES with a divisibility assert and a PhysX-buffer knob; grep stdout for PhysX overflow at rung 1; run rung 1 only on an idle GPU under systemd-run MemoryMax, no MPS while a campaign is live. Identical eval env for every arm; a process-floor pair before the screen (abort if |Δ| > R_eval).
